correctness.rationale: Operator norms computed by exact finite-row saturation; strict positivity of ℓ1 weights forces coordinatewise convergence of every scalar-norming sequence to one phase; the c0 target makes vanishing of the symbol sum necessary. Uniform convolution estimates for finite ramps, with ℓ1-dominated tails, give sufficiency in norm. The individual component is non-QNA for infinite support because each output coordinate of every image-ball limit lies strictly below the operator norm, whereas nonzero c0 vectors attain the supremum at a coordinate. An explicit phase-aligned ℓ1 perturbation gives the exact and attained relative distance. Real and complex cases, c=0 and strict norm gap examined. Finite tests are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: A complete infinite-dimensional, real-and-complex classification for a natural Wiener functional calculus graph family, governed by the intrinsic zero-frequency symbol evaluation. The exact attained ℓ1 correction cost and hyperplane stratification give quantitative stability/instability information. Opposite examples show the combined graph can fail QNA despite QNA coordinates and can achieve QNA with a nonQNA convolution coordinate, so it is not a name change, a finite enumeration, or a routine single instance. The result is related to, but does not claim to solve, range-sum density problems.
